title: Lockout, EMP & Terminal Overclock
youtubeTitle: Subspace Lattice Academy Ep.11 — Lockout, EMP & Terminal Overclock
description: Surgical Strike and Sector Integration are not the only finishes. Lockout awards the win when the opponent has zero legal replies — usually via Command Overload (EMP). When both fleets are lone Hubs, Terminal Overclock begins: Hub moves charge, drives fuse on fire, and the blast grows until a cowardly kite fails.

scenes.headline: Lockout, EMP & Terminal Overclock
scenes.subhead: Immobility is defeat — midgame EMP, then the lone-Hub runaway.
scenes.voiceover: Episode eleven: Lockout. Surgical Strike takes the Hub, and Sector Integration runs the clock. But there is a third engine win: leave the opponent with no legal moves. First the midgame EMP. Then Terminal Overclock, when only two flagships remain.

scenes.headline: The Lattice Escape Hatch
bullets: Cornered Hubs can capture to escape
Bodies alone cannot force zero moves
scenes.voiceover: Because the lattice has no chess-style 'check' rule, you cannot freeze a Hub just by surrounding it with ships. A cornered Command Hub will simply capture the piece blocking it to escape. To force zero moves, you have to kill their engines.

scenes.headline: Command Overload (EMP)
bullets: Charges only when your Hub is strictly stationary
Moving the Hub resets the charge to zero
Consumes your entire turn to fire
Seizes enemy engines in radius — your fleet is never in the blast
scenes.voiceover: Enter the EMP. Every turn you move a piece that is not your Command Hub, your EMP charges. Hold your ground. If your Hub moves even one square—or waffles back and forth—the charge resets to zero. When you fire, you spend the whole turn. Only enemy ships inside the blast freeze; your own fleet is never affected.

scenes.moveLabel: White EMP armed — one Escort still outside the blast
scenes.voiceover: Late game. White has anchored the Hub and charged EMP to fifteen. Black's Hub and one Escort sit inside the blast radius — but a second Black Escort still sits outside. Fire now and that escape hatch keeps Black alive.

scenes.moveLabel: White captures the Escort outside the blast
scenes.voiceover: White captures the outside Escort first. The Hub never moves, so the EMP stays armed. Now every remaining Black ship is inside the radius.

scenes.prompt: Black shuffled in vain. White spends the turn firing EMP. What happens to Black's legal replies?
scenes.voiceover: Pause and predict. Black's Hub shuffled but stayed inside the blast. White fires Command Overload — a full-turn action. What happens to Black's legal replies?
scenes.revealVoiceover: Black's engines die. For one reply ply, every enemy piece in the radius cannot move and cannot capture. White's own ships keep their engines — the cost was spending the turn.

scenes.voiceover: Because every remaining Black ship is inside the blast, the legal-move list is empty. The engine ends the game. Lockout.

scenes.headline: Terminal Overclock
bullets: Arms only when both fleets are lone Hubs
Hub moves charge EMP instead of resetting
Firing fuses your own drives — life support stays
Blast grows over time — kiting eventually fails
scenes.voiceover: Now the late endgame. When both fleets are stripped to lone Command Hubs, Terminal Overclock begins. Escort vents seal. Hub moves charge the EMP. Fire, and your own drives fuse — you cannot move again. That is not instant suicide: Lockout only checks whether the opponent still has a reply after your turn. If the blast empties their list, you win before your fused Hub would have to move. The terror is visible: the shared blast radius grows as the reactor runs away. Fleet default is plus one every five plies. This reel uses every three so you can see the bloom.

scenes.moveLabel: Both lone Hubs — Black outside r=3 at distance 4
scenes.voiceover: Mission five. Two naked flagships. Blast starts at radius three. Black sits at distance four — safely outside — and intends to stay there forever.
No escorts left to charge for you. White’s Hub itself steps — that is how Terminal EMP charges.
Black refuses contact. The coward slides sideways, still outside the old blast. Sensors already read the radiation climbing.

scenes.moveLabel: Thermal runaway — blast blooms to r=4
scenes.voiceover: White charges again. Shared age hits three. The shockwave blooms from three to four. Black is now on the edge of the field — the static kite is dying.

scenes.moveLabel: Black still plays the old geometry
scenes.voiceover: Black shuffles as if radius three were forever. The ambient field has already outgrown that lie.

scenes.moveLabel: White arms Terminal EMP 3/3 — Black inside r=4
scenes.voiceover: Third Hub move. EMP armed. Black remains at distance four — inside the grown radius. Firing earlier at three would have missed and fused White for nothing.
One last coward step. Nowhere left that radius four does not reach.

scenes.prompt: White fires Terminal Overclock. Own drives will fuse. Does Black still have a reply?
scenes.voiceover: Pause and predict. White fires Terminal Overclock — a full turn, own drives fuse. After that blast, does Black still have any legal reply?
scenes.revealVoiceover: No. Lockout only asks whether the opponent still has a move. Black's Hub is seized — zero replies — so White wins immediately. White's fused drives would matter on White's next turn, but that turn never comes: the game already ended when Black's list hit empty.

scenes.voiceover: Lockout. The firer is fused, but the engine never asked White for a reply — only Black. Endless kiting only bought time until thermal runaway blanketed the sector.

scenes.headline: Three wins. No soft draws.
scenes.voiceover: That is Lockout — midgame EMP when the fleet still stands, and Terminal Overclock when only Hubs remain. Anchor, charge, cut the escape hatch, or survive the runaway. Surgical Strike, Sector Integration, Lockout. You now have the complete manual.
